title: Balance Systems & Falls Assessment — From Romberg to TUG

hook.en: One fall can end an older person's independence. Learn how balance works, how to find which system is failing and which tests and exercises really prevent falls.
hook.ur: Ek fall kisi buzurg ki khud-mukhtari khatam kar sakti hai. Seekhein ke balance kaise kaam karta hai, kaun sa system fail ho raha hai kaise pata karein, aur kaun se tests aur exercises waqai falls rokte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain the three sensory systems of balance, interpret Romberg, TUG and Berg results and prescribe falls-prevention exercise at an effective dose.
goal.ur: End tak aap balance ke teen sensory systems samjha sakenge, Romberg, TUG aur Berg ke results parh sakenge aur falls-prevention exercise effective dose par likh sakenge.

text.en:
Balance means keeping your **centre of mass** over your **base of support**. The brain combines three sensory inputs:
**Vision** — where am I relative to the room?
**Vestibular** (inner ear) — is my head moving or tilting?
**Somatosensory** (proprioception, mainly feet and ankles) — what is the ground doing under me?
text.ur:
Balance ka matlab hai apna **centre of mass** **base of support** ke upar rakhna. Dimagh teen sensory inputs milata hai:
**Vision** — kamre ke hisaab se main kahan hoon?
**Vestibular** (andar ka kaan) — kya mera sir hil ya jhuk raha hai?
**Somatosensory** (proprioception, zyada tar pair aur ankles) — mere neeche zameen kya kar rahi hai?

simpler.en: Eyes, inner ears and feet send signals; the brain mixes them to keep you upright.
simpler.ur: Aankhein, andar ke kaan aur pair signals bhejte hain; dimagh unhein mila kar aap ko seedha rakhta hai.

text.en: Balance is a three-legged stool: vision, vestibular and feet. Lose one leg and you can still sit carefully on the other two. Lose two — say, numb feet in the dark — and you fall. That's why people with neuropathy fall at night.
text.ur: Balance teen taangon wala stool hai: vision, vestibular aur pair. Ek taang toot jaye to baqi do par ehtiyat se baith sakte hain. Do toot jayein — maslan andhere mein sunn pair — to aap gir jate hain. Isi liye neuropathy wale log raat ko girte hain.

text.en: **Romberg test:** feet together, arms by the side, first eyes open, then eyes closed (about 30 s). Positive = stable with eyes open but loses balance with eyes **closed**. It means the brain was relying on vision to replace poor **proprioception** (e.g. peripheral neuropathy, B12 deficiency, dorsal column disease). In cerebellar ataxia, balance is poor even with eyes open, so Romberg is not 'positive' in the classic sense.
text.ur: **Romberg test:** pair jor kar, haath side par, pehle aankhein khuli, phir band (taqreeban 30 s). Positive = aankhein khuli hon to stable lekin **band** hon to balance kho dena. Matlab dimagh kamzor **proprioception** ki jagah vision par bharosa kar raha tha (maslan peripheral neuropathy, B12 ki kami, dorsal column disease). Cerebellar ataxia mein aankhein khuli hone par bhi balance kharab hota hai, is liye classic maani mein Romberg 'positive' nahi hota.

question.en: A diabetic man stands steadily with eyes open but sways and steps within 5 seconds of closing his eyes. Which system is most likely impaired?
question.ur: Diabetic aadmi aankhein khuli hon to mazbooti se khara hai lekin aankhein band karne ke 5 second mein jhoolta aur qadam utha leta hai. Kaun sa system sab se zyada kamzor hone ka imkaan?

text.en: Somatosensory — peripheral neuropathy
text.ur: Somatosensory — peripheral neuropathy

feedback.en: Yes — a positive Romberg with diabetes points to loss of foot proprioception. Check sensation and footwear, and warn about the dark.
feedback.ur: Haan — diabetes ke saath positive Romberg pair ki proprioception ki kami batata hai. Sensation aur jootay check karein, aur andhere se khabardar karein.

text.en: Cerebellum
text.ur: Cerebellum

feedback.en: Cerebellar problems cause unsteadiness even with the eyes open.
feedback.ur: Cerebellar masle aankhein khuli hone par bhi be-qarari dete hain.

text.en: Vision
text.ur: Vision

feedback.en: He was stable while using vision — vision is what's compensating.
feedback.ur: Vision istemal karte hue woh stable tha — vision hi to compensate kar raha hai.

rows.en: Ankle
rows.ur: Ankle

rows.en: Small, slow sway on a firm, wide surface
rows.ur: Sakht, chauri surface par chhota, aahista jhoolna

rows.en: Body moves as one unit around the ankles
rows.ur: Jism ek unit ki tarah ankles ke gird hilta hai

rows.en: Hip
rows.ur: Hip

rows.en: Larger or faster sway, narrow surface
rows.ur: Bara ya tez jhoolna, tang surface

rows.en: Bending at the hips to move the trunk
rows.ur: Trunk hilane ke liye hips se jhukna

rows.en: Stepping
rows.ur: Stepping

rows.en: Centre of mass moves outside the base of support
rows.ur: Centre of mass base of support se bahar chala jaye

rows.en: A quick step or grab to make a new base
rows.ur: Naya base banane ke liye tez qadam ya pakarna

rows.en: Timed Up and Go (TUG)
rows.ur: Timed Up and Go (TUG)

rows.en: Stand up from a chair, walk 3 m, turn, walk back, sit — usual pace and aid
rows.ur: Kursi se uthein, 3 m chalein, murein, wapas aa kar baith jayein — aam raftaar aur aid ke saath

rows.en: ≥ 12–13.5 s in community-dwelling older adults (use with other findings)
rows.ur: Community mein rehne wale buzurgon mein ≥ 12–13.5 s (doosri findings ke saath)

rows.en: Berg Balance Scale
rows.ur: Berg Balance Scale

rows.en: 14 tasks scored 0–4 (max 56)
rows.ur: 14 kaam, har ek 0–4 (zyada se zyada 56)

rows.en: Score below about 45/56
rows.ur: Score taqreeban 45/56 se kam

rows.en: 30-second chair stand
rows.ur: 30-second chair stand

rows.en: Full stands in 30 s, arms crossed
rows.ur: 30 s mein poore khare hona, baazu cross

rows.en: Below age norms — e.g. < 12 at ages 60–64
rows.ur: Umar ke norms se kam — maslan 60–64 saal mein < 12

rows.en: 4-stage balance test
rows.ur: 4-stage balance test

rows.en: Feet together → semi-tandem → tandem → one leg, 10 s each
rows.ur: Pair saath → semi-tandem → tandem → ek taang, har ek 10 s

rows.en: Can't hold tandem stance for 10 s
rows.ur: Tandem stance 10 s na pakar sakein

question.en: A 74-year-old completes the TUG in 18 seconds and needs her hands to stand up. What is the best interpretation?
question.ur: 74 saal ki khatoon TUG 18 second mein karti hain aur uthne ke liye haathon ka sahara leti hain. Behtareen interpretation?

text.en: Normal for her age
text.ur: Umar ke hisaab se normal

feedback.en: 18 s is well above common risk cut-offs, and needing the hands suggests leg weakness.
feedback.ur: 18 s aam risk cut-offs se kaafi upar hai, aur haathon ka sahara taangon ki kamzori batata hai.

text.en: Increased falls risk — do a fuller falls assessment and start strength and balance training
text.ur: Falls risk zyada — mukammal falls assessment karein aur strength aur balance training shuru karein

feedback.en: Yes — combine with history (previous falls, medicines, vision, home) for a full picture.
feedback.ur: Haan — mukammal tasveer ke liye history (pichli falls, dawaiyan, nazar, ghar) ke saath milayein.

text.en: She must stop walking outside
text.ur: Unhein bahar chalna band karna chahiye

feedback.en: Restricting activity speeds deconditioning — improve capacity and safety instead.
feedback.ur: Activity rokne se kamzori tez hoti hai — iske bajaye capacity aur safety behtar karein.

text.en: A **multifactorial falls assessment** asks: previous falls and near-falls, fear of falling, medicines (sedatives, antidepressants, blood-pressure drugs, many medicines together), **orthostatic hypotension** (BP lying then standing), vision, feet and footwear, continence (rushing to the toilet at night), cognition and home hazards (loose rugs, poor lighting, wet bathroom floors, stairs without rails).
text.ur: **Multifactorial falls assessment** poochti hai: pichli falls aur girte girte bachna, girne ka dar, dawaiyan (sedatives, antidepressants, blood-pressure ki dawaiyan, ek saath bohat si dawaiyan), **orthostatic hypotension** (BP lait kar phir khare ho kar), nazar, pair aur jootay, continence (raat ko toilet ki taraf jaldi), yaaddasht aur ghar ke khatre (dheeli darriyan, kam roshni, geela bathroom floor, railing ke baghair seerhiyan).

text.en: Exercise that **challenges balance** reduces the rate of falls in community-dwelling older people by about a quarter, and programmes with a high balance challenge and **more than about 3 hours per week** in total have the biggest effect (Sherrington, Cochrane 2019). Walking alone is not enough; strength plus progressive balance practice is the core. Tai chi is also effective.
text.ur: **Balance ko challenge** karne wali exercise community mein rehne wale buzurgon mein falls ki rate taqreeban ek chauthai kam karti hai, aur zyada balance challenge aur kul mila kar **hafte mein taqreeban 3 ghante se zyada** wale programmes ka asar sab se bara hai (Sherrington, Cochrane 2019). Sirf walking kaafi nahi; strength aur progressive balance practice markaz hain. Tai chi bhi effective hai.

prompt.en: Does each exercise truly challenge balance?
prompt.ur: Kya har exercise waqai balance ko challenge karti hai?

text.en: Tandem walking along a line
text.ur: Line par tandem walking

text.en: Seated knee extensions
text.ur: Baith kar knee extensions

why.en: Builds strength, but seated — no balance demand.
why.ur: Strength banati hai, lekin baith kar — balance ki demand nahi.

text.en: Standing on one leg near a counter
text.ur: Counter ke paas ek taang par khare hona

why.en: Small base, safe support close by.

text.en: Reaching outside the base of support in standing
text.ur: Khare ho kar base of support se bahar haath barhana

why.en: Moves the centre of mass towards the limits of stability.
why.ur: Centre of mass ko stability ki had tak le jata hai.

text.en: Lying-down ankle pumps
text.ur: Lait kar ankle pumps

why.en: Good for circulation, no balance demand.
why.ur: Circulation ke liye acha, balance ki demand nahi.

text.en: Urgent signs: **sudden** loss of balance with new weakness, facial droop, slurred speech, double vision or severe headache — think **stroke** and call emergency services. A fall with hip pain and inability to bear weight — suspect **hip fracture**. Repeated unexplained falls or blackouts need medical review (heart rhythm, blood pressure). Always teach how to get up from the floor or call for help.
text.ur: Urgent nishaniyan: nayi kamzori, chehra latakna, zabaan larkharana, double vision ya shadeed sar dard ke saath **achanak** balance kho dena — **stroke** sochein aur emergency ko call karein. Girne ke baad hip mein dard aur wazan na utha sakna — **hip fracture** ka shak. Baar baar be-wajah girna ya behoshi medical review maangti hai (dil ki dhadkan, blood pressure). Hamesha sikhayein ke zameen se kaise uthein ya madad kaise bulayein.

question.en: Which programme best follows the falls-prevention evidence for a fit-enough 70-year-old?
question.ur: Kaafi had tak fit 70 saal ke insaan ke liye kaun sa programme falls-prevention evidence ke sab se qareeb hai?

text.en: A daily 20-minute walk only
text.ur: Sirf rozana 20 minute ki walk

feedback.en: Healthy, but walking alone doesn't reliably reduce falls.
feedback.ur: Sehatmand, lekin sirf walking falls ko yaqeeni tor par kam nahi karti.

text.en: Progressive balance and leg-strength exercises, about 3+ hours a week in total, continued long-term
text.ur: Progressive balance aur taangon ki strength exercises, hafte mein kul taqreeban 3+ ghante, lambe arse tak

feedback.en: Yes — high balance challenge, adequate dose and continuation are what work.
feedback.ur: Haan — zyada balance challenge, munasib dose aur jaari rakhna hi kaam karta hai.

text.en: Seated stretches twice a week
text.ur: Hafte mein do dafa baith kar stretches

feedback.en: No balance challenge and too low a dose.
feedback.ur: Balance challenge nahi aur dose bohat kam.

text.en: Match training to the failing system: poor proprioception — standing and stepping on varied surfaces, with vision as a safety net at first; vestibular hypofunction — gaze-stability and head-movement exercises (refer BPPV for repositioning); poor strength — progressive sit-to-stands, step-ups and heel raises. Always progress from stable to less stable, slow to fast, and single-task to dual-task (e.g. walking while counting backwards).
text.ur: Training ko fail hone wale system ke mutabiq rakhein: kamzor proprioception — mukhtalif surfaces par khare hona aur qadam rakhna, shuru mein vision ko safety net bana kar; vestibular hypofunction — gaze-stability aur sir hilane ki exercises (BPPV ho to repositioning ke liye); kamzor strength — progressive sit-to-stands, step-ups aur heel raises. Hamesha stable se kam stable, aahista se tez, aur single-task se dual-task tak progress karein (maslan ulti ginti karte hue chalna).

text.en: Common mistakes: balance exercises that aren't challenging (seated or holding on with both hands throughout); stopping after a few weeks; ignoring medicines, blood pressure and home hazards; and advising someone to 'stay in bed to be safe' — which weakens them and increases falls.
text.ur: Aam ghaltiyan: aisi balance exercises jo challenge na karein (baith kar ya poora waqt dono haathon se pakar kar); kuch hafton baad rok dena; dawaiyon, blood pressure aur ghar ke khatron ko nazarandaz karna; aur kisi ko 'safe rehne ke liye bed par rahein' kehna — jo usay kamzor aur girne ka khatra zyada karta hai.

question.en: Plan the first session for an 80-year-old who has fallen twice at night going to the toilet.
question.ur: 80 saal ke insaan ke liye pehla session plan karein jo raat ko toilet jate hue do dafa gira hai.

answer.en: Assess: falls history, lying/standing BP, medicines (sedatives, diuretics), vision, foot sensation and Romberg, strength (30-s chair stand), TUG and a 4-stage balance test. Act: night-light and clear path to the toilet, sit on the bed edge for a moment before standing, footwear review, practise getting up from the floor. Start a progressive strength-and-balance home programme and ask the doctor to review medicines and night-time urination.
answer.ur: Assess: falls ki history, lait kar/khare ho kar BP, dawaiyan (sedatives, diuretics), nazar, pair ki sensation aur Romberg, strength (30-s chair stand), TUG aur 4-stage balance test. Amal: night-light aur toilet tak saaf raasta, khare hone se pehle thori dair bed ke kinare baithna, jooton ka jaiza, zameen se uthne ki practice. Progressive strength-and-balance home programme shuru karein aur doctor se dawaiyon aur raat ke peshaab ka review karwayein.

summary.en: Balance combines vision, vestibular and somatosensory input; a positive Romberg (worse with eyes closed) points to poor proprioception.
summary.ur: Balance vision, vestibular aur somatosensory input milata hai; positive Romberg (aankhein band par badtar) kamzor proprioception batata hai.

summary.en: Use TUG, Berg, the 30-s chair stand and the 4-stage balance test within a multifactorial falls assessment.
summary.ur: TUG, Berg, 30-s chair stand aur 4-stage balance test ko multifactorial falls assessment ke andar istemal karein.

summary.en: Falls prevention works with progressive balance and strength training at about 3+ hours a week, continued long-term.
summary.ur: Falls prevention progressive balance aur strength training se kaam karti hai, hafte mein taqreeban 3+ ghante, lambe arse tak.

front.en: What does a positive Romberg test mean?

back.en: Stable with eyes open but not closed — proprioceptive (sensory) loss, not cerebellar.
back.ur: Aankhein khuli par stable lekin band par nahi — proprioceptive (sensory) kami, cerebellar nahi.

front.en: Common TUG cut-off for higher falls risk in older adults?
front.ur: Buzurgon mein zyada falls risk ke liye aam TUG cut-off?

back.ur: Taqreeban ≥ 12–13.5 second (doosri findings ke saath parhein).

front.en: Berg Balance Scale maximum and common risk cut-off?
front.ur: Berg Balance Scale ka maximum aur aam risk cut-off?

back.en: 56; below about 45 suggests higher falls risk.
back.ur: 56; taqreeban 45 se kam zyada falls risk batata hai.

back.en: Progressive, highly challenging balance (+ strength) training, about 3+ hours per week in total, continued.
back.ur: Progressive, zyada challenge wali balance (+ strength) training, hafte mein kul taqreeban 3+ ghante, jaari.

note.en: Practise TUG, Berg and more step by step.
note.ur: TUG, Berg aur mazeed qadam ba qadam practise karein.

note.en: Programme design and dosing in detail.
note.ur: Programme design aur dose tafseel se.

note.en: When the vestibular leg of the stool fails.
note.ur: Jab stool ki vestibular taang kamzor ho.
